source.text: Ἰάκωβος θεοῦ καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος ταῖς δώδεκα φυλαῖς ταῖς ἐν τῇ διασπορᾷ χαίρειν.

records.literal_gloss: James, of God and of Lord Jesus Christ slave, to the twelve tribes the [ones] in the dispersion, to rejoice.

en.L: James, a slave of God and of [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion: greetings.
en.B: From James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. To the twelve tribes scattered among the nations: greetings.
en.R: This letter is from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. I am writing to the twelve tribes of God's people, who are scattered across many lands. Greetings!

es.L: Santiago, esclavo de Dios y [del] Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, a las doce tribus [que están] en la dispersión: saludos.
es.B: De Santiago, siervo de Dios y del Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. A las doce tribus dispersas entre las naciones: saludos.
es.R: Esta carta es de Santiago, siervo de Dios y del Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Escribo a las doce tribus del pueblo de Dios, que viven dispersas por muchas tierras. ¡Saludos!

sw.L: Yakobo, mtumwa wa Mungu na wa Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kwa makabila kumi na mawili yaliyo katika utawanyiko: salamu.
sw.B: Kutoka kwa Yakobo, mtumishi wa Mungu na wa Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Kwa makabila kumi na mawili yaliyotawanyika kati ya mataifa: salamu.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa Yakobo, mtumishi wa Mungu na wa Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Ninawaandikia makabila kumi na mawili ya watu wa Mungu, ambao wametawanyika katika nchi nyingi. Salamu!

decisions.choice: slave: someone wholly owned by and at the service of a master
decisions.reason: δοῦλος is the ordinary word for a slave. James claims no title but belonging to God and to Jesus. In Israel's Scriptures "slave of the Lord" was also an honored name for Moses, David and the prophets (Joshua 1:2; Jeremiah 7:25), so the word is humble and honorable at once.

decisions.choice: two persons are named: God, and the Lord Jesus Christ
alternatives: one person: Jesus Christ, who is God and Lord
decisions.reason: "God" and "Lord" are joined by "and" with no article, and the usual way to read the phrase is "God and the Lord Jesus Christ", as in the openings of Paul's letters (Philippians 1:2). Setting Jesus beside God as the master James serves is already a high claim.

decisions.choice: the twelve tribes in the dispersion: God's people living outside the land of Israel
alternatives: Christians everywhere, as the new Israel (Galatians 6:16; 1 Peter 1:1)
Jews in general, believers or not
decisions.reason: διασπορά was the name for the Jewish communities scattered beyond the land since the exiles (John 7:35). "Twelve tribes" calls the readers Israel as God's whole people. The letter assumes they believe in Jesus (2:1), so it is most likely written to Jewish believers outside the land; it may also address the church as God's people scattered in the world.

decisions.choice: greetings: the standard opening word of a Greek letter
decisions.reason: χαίρω ("to rejoice") is how Greek letters said "greetings" (Acts 15:23, also from James). The next word of the letter, "joy" (χαρὰν), picks up the same root.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: scattered among the nations; scattered across many lands
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the dispersion" means rather than use a technical term. Readable also says who the twelve tribes are (God's people).

decisions.choice: Santiago
decisions.reason: "Santiago" is the usual Spanish name of this James and of his letter ("la carta de Santiago"). "Jacobo" is closer to the Greek form but is the name Spanish Bibles keep for the patriarch Jacob's line and is unfamiliar for the author.

decisions.choice: siervo
decisions.reason: "Siervo" in Balanced and Readable, as in the English and the style guide; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "esclavo".

decisions.choice: mtumishi
decisions.reason: "Mtumishi" in Balanced and Readable, as in the English and the style guide; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "mtumwa".

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: Πᾶσαν χαρὰν ἡγήσασθε, ἀδελφοί μου, ὅταν πειρασμοῖς περιπέσητε ποικίλοις, γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν·

records.literal_gloss: All joy consider [it], brothers of me, when trials you fall into various, \v 3 knowing that the testing of you of the faith produces endurance;

en.L: Consider [it] all joy, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, whenever you fall into various trials, \v 3 knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance;
en.B: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, whenever you find yourselves in trials of every sort, regard it as a reason for great joy, \v 3 because you know that the testing your faith goes through produces endurance.
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, all sorts of hard times will come to you. When they do, be full of joy. \v 3 You know that when your faith is tested, the testing builds endurance in you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Considérenlo|Consideradlo}} todo gozo, hermanos míos, cuando {{plural_you:caigan|caigáis}} en pruebas diversas, \v 3 sabiendo que la prueba de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe produce perseverancia;
es.B: Hermanos míos, cuando {{plural_you:se encuentren|os encontréis}} en pruebas de toda clase, {{plural_you:ténganlo|tenedlo}} por motivo de gran gozo, \v 3 porque {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que la prueba por la que pasa {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe produce perseverancia.
es.R: Hermanos míos, {{plural_you:les|os}} vendrán dificultades de muchas clases. Cuando lleguen, {{plural_you:estén|estad}} llenos de alegría. \v 3 {{plural_you:Ya saben|Ya sabéis}} que, cuando {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe es puesta a prueba, esa prueba hace crecer en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la perseverancia.

sw.L: Hesabuni kuwa ni furaha kamili, ndugu zangu, kila mnapoingia katika majaribu ya kila aina, \v 3 mkitambua kwamba kupimwa kwa imani yenu hutokeza ustahimilivu;
sw.B: Ndugu zangu, kila mnapojikuta katika majaribu ya kila namna, yaoneni kuwa sababu ya furaha kubwa, \v 3 kwa maana mnajua kwamba imani yenu inapopimwa, upimaji huo hutokeza ustahimilivu.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, mtapatwa na taabu za aina nyingi. Zikiwajia, furahini sana. \v 3 Mnajua kwamba imani yenu inapojaribiwa, majaribu hayo huwajenga ili mweze kustahimili zaidi.

decisions.choice: trials: hardships that put faith to the test
decisions.reason: πειρασμός can mean a test or a temptation. Here it is something one "falls into" from outside, and verse 3 calls it the testing of faith, so it means hardship and trouble. In verses 13-14 James turns to the inner pull toward sin, using the verb from the same family.

decisions.choice: all joy: nothing but joy, joy in full
decisions.reason: "All" with "joy" means joy without remainder. James does not call trials pleasant; he tells the readers how to reckon them (ἡγέομαι, "consider, count") because of what they produce (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the testing of your faith: the process that proves faith genuine
alternatives: what is genuine in your faith, once tested
decisions.reason: δοκίμιον is the testing by which metal is proved (Proverbs 27:21). 1 Peter 1:7 uses the same word for faith tested like gold. Here it is the testing itself that produces something.

decisions.choice: endurance: holding firm under pressure without giving way
decisions.reason: ὑπομονή is an active quality: staying under a load and not giving up. It is more than waiting quietly. James comes back to it in 1:12 and 5:11 (Job).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James addresses the whole church, men and women, so the gender setting applies; the traditional "brothers" is the alternative.

decisions.choice: endurance
decisions.reason: "Endurance" is used at every level for this word and its verb in James (1:4, 1:12, 5:11), so the thread of the letter can be followed; "patience" sounds too passive.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, as in Romans and Philippians, so the plural has no gender setting in this letter.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: James writes to the churches in the plural throughout. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain).

decisions.choice: perseverancia
decisions.reason: "Paciencia" is the traditional word but sounds passive, and the meaning decision describes an active holding firm. "Perseverancia" (and the verb "perseverar" in 1:12) is used for this word family throughout the letter, as in Romans.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" and "mtu" already mean brothers and sisters, any person, and Swahili pronouns have no gender, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili in this chapter.

decisions.choice: majaribu; kupimwa
decisions.reason: "Majaribu" is the hardships (verse 2); for the testing of faith (verse 3) Literal and Balanced say "kupimwa", the word for testing metal or weighing, which is the picture of the Greek word (see the meaning decision). Readable keeps the simpler "inapojaribiwa".

decisions.choice: ustahimilivu
decisions.reason: "Saburi" is the traditional word but sounds like quiet waiting. "Ustahimilivu" (and the verb "kustahimili") is holding out under a load, as the meaning decision says, and is used for this word family throughout the letter, as in Romans 2:7.

source.text: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ ἔργον τέλειον ἐχέτω, ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι, ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι.

records.literal_gloss: And the endurance work perfect let have, so that you may be perfect and whole, in nothing lacking.

en.L: And let endurance have [its] perfect work, so that you may be perfect and whole, falling short in nothing.
en.B: Let endurance carry its work through to the end, so that you may be mature and whole, with nothing missing.
en.R: Keep on enduring until endurance has finished its work in you. Then you will be fully grown and whole, with nothing missing.

es.L: Y que la perseverancia tenga [su] obra perfecta, para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} perfectos y cabales, sin que {{plural_you:les|os}} falte nada.
es.B: {{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} que la perseverancia lleve su obra hasta el final, para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} maduros y completos, sin que {{plural_you:les|os}} falte nada.
es.R: {{plural_you:Sigan|Seguid}} perseverando hasta que la perseverancia termine su obra en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Entonces {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} personas maduras y completas, sin que {{plural_you:les|os}} falte nada.

sw.L: Na ustahimilivu uwe na kazi iliyo kamilifu, ili mwe wakamilifu na kamili, mkiwa hampungukiwi na kitu chochote.
sw.B: Acheni ustahimilivu ukamilishe kazi yake, ili mkomae na kuwa kamili, bila kukosa chochote.
sw.R: Endeleeni kustahimili mpaka ustahimilivu umalize kazi yake ndani yenu. Ndipo mtakuwa mmekomaa kabisa na kamili, bila kukosa chochote.

decisions.choice: perfect: complete, fully grown, having reached its goal
decisions.reason: τέλειος means brought to its goal. Endurance must do its "perfect" (complete) work so that the readers become "perfect" (mature) people; the word is repeated on purpose. James uses it again of God's gift (1:17), the law (1:25) and the person who controls the tongue (3:2).

decisions.choice: whole: sound in every part
decisions.reason: ὁλόκληρος describes something with all its parts present and sound. With "lacking in nothing" it pictures a life with no part missing.

decisions.choice: lacking: the word that leads into verse 5
decisions.reason: "Lacking in nothing" (λειπόμενοι) is picked up at once by "if any of you lacks" (λείπεται). James often links his sayings by repeating a word.

decisions.choice: mature; fully grown (for the second "perfect")
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "perfect" twice to show the repetition. Balanced and Readable say "mature" and "fully grown" for the people, because "perfect" in everyday English suggests being without fault.

decisions.choice: kupungukiwa (L); kukosa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for "lacking" here is picked up at once in verse 5 (see the meaning decision). Each level uses one verb in both verses: "hampungukiwi" / "amepungukiwa" at Literal, "bila kukosa" / "anakosa" at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: Εἰ δέ τις ὑμῶν λείπεται σοφίας, αἰτείτω παρὰ τοῦ διδόντος θεοῦ πᾶσιν ἁπλῶς καὶ μὴ ὀνειδίζοντος, καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: And if anyone of you lacks wisdom, let him ask from the giving God to all generously and not reproaching, and it will be given to him;

en.L: And if anyone of you lacks wisdom, let {{gender:them|him}} ask from the God who gives to all generously and without reproaching, and it will be given to {{gender:them|him}};
en.B: If any of you is short of wisdom, ask God, who gives to everyone with an open hand and without scolding, and it will be given to you.
en.R: Do any of you need wisdom? Then ask God for it. God gives freely to everyone, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not scold people for asking. He will give you wisdom.

es.L: Y si a alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} le falta sabiduría, que [la] pida al Dios que da a todos con generosidad y sin reprochar, y le será dada;
es.B: Si a alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} le falta sabiduría, que se la pida a Dios, que da a todos con mano abierta y sin reprender, y se le dará.
es.R: ¿Alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} necesita sabiduría? Que se la pida a Dios. Dios da con gusto a todos, y no regaña a nadie por pedir. Dios le dará sabiduría.

sw.L: Na kama yeyote kati yenu amepungukiwa na hekima, aombe kwa Mungu anayewapa wote kwa moyo mkunjufu bila kulaumu, naye atapewa;
sw.B: Ikiwa mmoja wenu anakosa hekima, amwombe Mungu, anayewapa watu wote kwa mkono wazi bila kuwasuta, naye atapewa.
sw.R: Je, kuna yeyote kati yenu anayehitaji hekima? Basi amwombe Mungu. Mungu huwapa wote kwa moyo mkunjufu, wala hamkaripii mtu yeyote kwa kuomba. Atampa hekima.

decisions.choice: wisdom: the skill of living rightly before God
decisions.reason: In Israel's wisdom books wisdom is practical and comes from God (Proverbs 2:6). James later describes "the wisdom from above" by the way it behaves (3:13-18). Here it is what is needed to meet trials well.

decisions.choice: generously: wholeheartedly, without holding back
decisions.reason: ἁπλῶς means "simply, without division". Said of a giver, it means giving freely and with an undivided heart. It stands against the divided person of verse 8, who asks with two minds.

decisions.choice: without reproaching: God does not taunt or shame the one who asks
decisions.reason: ὀνειδίζω means to reproach or insult. God does not hold the asking against anyone or throw past failures back at them.

decisions.choice: it will be given: God is the giver
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God as the one who gives, as in Jesus' saying "Ask, and it will be given to you" (Matthew 7:7). Solomon's request for wisdom (1 Kings 3:9-12) is the classic picture.

decisions.choice: you (second person)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak directly to "you", as "any of you" invites, instead of the third-person command; the meaning is the same and the gender setting is not needed.

decisions.choice: He will give you wisdom
alternatives: it will be given to you
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver (see the meaning decision on the passive) and repeats what is given.

decisions.choice: third person kept ("que se la pida", "le")
alternatives: second person, as the English Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable turn to "you" to avoid a gendered pronoun. Spanish verbs and "le" do not mark gender, so the Spanish keeps James's third-person command ("alguno de ustedes ... que se la pida") at every level here and in verses 6-8, with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: third person kept ("amwombe", "atapewa")
alternatives: second person, as the English Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Swahili verbs do not mark gender, so the Swahili keeps James's third-person command ("mmoja wenu ... amwombe Mungu") at every level here and in verses 6-8, where the English Balanced and Readable turn to "you".

source.text: αἰτείτω δὲ ἐν πίστει, μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικεν κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ·

records.literal_gloss: But let him ask in faith, nothing doubting, for the [one] doubting is like a wave of sea being driven by wind and being tossed;

en.L: But let {{gender:them|him}} ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of [the] sea, driven by wind and tossed about;
en.B: But you must ask in faith, without wavering. Anyone who wavers is like a wave out at sea, driven by the wind and thrown this way and that.
en.R: But when you ask, ask with faith, and do not doubt. A person who doubts is like a wave on the sea. The wind blows it and pushes it around.

es.L: Pero pida con fe, sin dudar en nada, pues el que duda se parece a una ola del mar, llevada por el viento y sacudida;
es.B: Pero ha de pedir con fe, sin vacilar. Quien vacila es como una ola en alta mar, que el viento arrastra y lanza de aquí para allá.
es.R: Pero cuando pida, que pida con fe y sin dudar. Quien duda es como una ola del mar. El viento sopla sobre ella y la empuja de un lado a otro.

sw.L: Lakini aombe kwa imani, bila kutilia shaka chochote, kwa maana anayetilia shaka ni kama wimbi la bahari linalosukumwa na upepo na kurushwa-rushwa;
sw.B: Lakini aombe kwa imani, bila kusitasita. Mtu anayesitasita ni kama wimbi la bahari kuu, linalosukumwa na upepo na kutupwa huku na huku.
sw.R: Lakini anapoomba, aombe kwa imani, bila kuwa na shaka. Mtu mwenye shaka ni kama wimbi la baharini. Upepo unalipiga na kulisukuma huku na huku.

decisions.choice: doubting: divided in oneself, wavering between trusting God and not
decisions.reason: διακρίνω in the middle voice means to be at odds with oneself. Verse 8 explains it as being "double-minded". The problem is not a question in the mind but a divided loyalty (compare Matthew 21:21; Romans 4:20).

decisions.choice: faith: trust in God as the generous giver of verse 5
decisions.reason: Faith here is the confidence that God gives freely and without reproach, the same faith that is tested in verse 3.

decisions.choice: a wave driven and tossed by the wind: no steady course
decisions.reason: The wave goes wherever the wind pushes it. Isaiah 57:20 and Ephesians 4:14 use the restless sea in the same way.

decisions.choice: wavering, wavers
decisions.reason: Balanced says "waver" because the word means being pulled two ways, not having doubts about ideas; Literal and Readable keep "doubt".

decisions.choice: you must ask; when you ask
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable go on speaking to "you", as in verse 5.

source.text: μὴ γὰρ οἰέσθω ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὅτι λήμψεταί τι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἀνὴρ δίψυχος, ἀκατάστατος ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: for not let suppose the man that that he will receive anything from the Lord, \v 8 a man double-souled, unstable in all the ways of him.

en.L: For let {{gender:that person|that man}} not suppose that {{gender:they|he}} will receive anything from the Lord, \v 8 [being] {{gender:a double-minded person|a double-minded man}}, unstable in all {{gender:their|his}} ways.
en.B: {{gender:Such a person|Such a man}} must not expect to receive anything from the Lord. \v 8 {{gender:They are|He is}} of two minds and unsteady in all {{gender:they do|he does}}.
en.R: A person like that should not think the Lord will give {{gender:them|him}} anything. \v 8 {{gender:They are|He is}} pulled two ways at once, and nothing {{gender:they do|he does}} is steady.

es.L: Porque no piense {{gender:esa persona|ese hombre}} que recibirá cosa alguna del Señor, \v 8 [siendo] {{gender:una persona|un hombre}} de doble ánimo, inestable en todos sus caminos.
es.B: {{gender:Una persona así|Un hombre así}} no debe esperar recibir nada del Señor. \v 8 Tiene el ánimo dividido y es inestable en todo lo que hace.
es.R: {{gender:Una persona así|Un hombre así}} no debe pensar que el Señor le dará algo. \v 8 Su corazón tira hacia dos lados a la vez, y nada de lo que hace es firme.

sw.L: Kwa maana mtu huyo asifikiri kwamba atapata chochote kutoka kwa Bwana, \v 8 [akiwa] mtu mwenye nia mbili, asiye imara katika njia zake zote.
sw.B: Mtu wa namna hiyo asitarajie kupokea chochote kutoka kwa Bwana. \v 8 Yeye ni mwenye nia mbili, hana msimamo katika yote anayofanya.
sw.R: Mtu kama huyo asifikiri kwamba Bwana atampa chochote. \v 8 Moyo wake unavutwa pande mbili kwa wakati mmoja, na hakuna anachofanya kilicho imara.

decisions.choice: double-minded: with a divided loyalty to God
decisions.reason: δίψυχος is literally "two-souled". The word is not known from Greek writing before James, who uses it again in 4:8 ("purify your hearts, you double-minded"). It echoes Israel's warnings against a divided heart (Psalm 12:2; 1 Kings 18:21) and stands against the "whole" person of verse 4.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, the giver of verse 5
decisions.reason: The one who "gives to all generously" in verse 5 is God, so "the Lord" here is God. James uses the title for both God and Jesus (1:1).

decisions.choice: verse 8 describes the same person, in apposition
alternatives: a separate saying: "a double-minded man is unstable in all his ways"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuation keeps verse 8 inside the sentence: it describes "that person". Read as a separate proverb it says much the same thing.

decisions.choice: all his ways: everything he does, his whole conduct
decisions.reason: "Ways" for the course of a person's life and conduct is a common biblical idiom (Psalm 1:6; Proverbs 3:6).

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|that man}}; {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: James's "man" here is anyone who asks with a divided heart, so the gender setting gives an inclusive default with the traditional wording as the alternative.

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|ese hombre}}; {{gender:una persona|un hombre}}
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish puts the gender span on the noun ("persona" or "hombre") and on any word that must agree with it. Spanish verb endings, "su" and "le" do not show gender, and words agreeing with "alguien", "quien" or "cada uno" take the ordinary inclusive form, so they need no span. Spanish therefore has fewer gender spans than English in this chapter.

decisions.choice: tiene el ánimo dividido; su corazón tira hacia dos lados
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "de doble ánimo", the literal picture of the Greek word. Balanced and Readable say the same with "ánimo dividido" and a picture of being pulled two ways, avoiding adjectives that would need to agree with "persona" or "hombre".

source.text: Καυχάσθω δὲ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ, ὁ δὲ πλούσιος ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου παρελεύσεται.

records.literal_gloss: And let boast the brother the lowly in the height of him, \v 10 and the rich in the lowering of him, because like a flower of grass he will pass away.

en.L: And let the lowly {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} boast in {{gender:their|his}} exaltation, \v 10 and the rich in {{gender:their|his}} lowering, because like a flower of [the] grass {{gender:they|he}} will pass away.
en.B: The {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} of low position should take pride in being lifted high, \v 10 and the rich person in being brought low, because the rich will pass away like a wild flower.
en.R: A {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} who is poor and looked down on should be proud that God has lifted {{gender:them|him}} up. \v 10 And a rich person should be proud of being made low, because rich people will be gone, just like a flower in the grass.

es.L: Y gloríese {{gender:el hermano o la hermana|el hermano}} de condición humilde en su exaltación, \v 10 y el rico en su humillación, porque como flor de [la] hierba pasará.
es.B: {{gender:El hermano o la hermana|El hermano}} de condición humilde debe sentir orgullo de su alta posición, \v 10 y el rico, de verse rebajado, porque el rico pasará como una flor silvestre.
es.R: {{gender:El hermano o la hermana|El hermano}} que es pobre y a quien la gente desprecia debe sentir orgullo, porque Dios le ha dado un lugar alto. \v 10 Y el rico debe sentir orgullo de ser rebajado, porque los ricos desaparecerán, igual que una flor en el campo.

sw.L: Na ndugu aliye wa hali ya chini ajivunie kuinuliwa kwake, \v 10 na tajiri [ajivunie] kushushwa kwake, kwa sababu atapita kama ua la nyasi.
sw.B: Ndugu aliye wa hali ya chini na ajivunie kuinuliwa juu, \v 10 na tajiri ajivunie kushushwa chini, kwa sababu tajiri atapita kama ua la porini.
sw.R: Ndugu aliye maskini na kudharauliwa na watu ajivunie kwamba Mungu amemwinua. \v 10 Na tajiri ajivunie kushushwa chini, kwa sababu matajiri watatoweka kama ua katika nyasi.

decisions.choice: lowly: low in social and economic standing, poor
decisions.reason: ταπεινός here is set against "the rich", so it means someone low in the world's eyes, not a humble frame of mind. James returns to the poor whom God has chosen in 2:5.

decisions.choice: exaltation and lowering: God reverses the world's ranking
decisions.reason: The poor believer's high place is the standing God gives (2:5); the rich person's lowering is the truth that wealth and life pass away (verse 11). Scripture often speaks of God lifting the lowly and bringing down the proud (1 Samuel 2:7; Luke 1:52).

decisions.choice: the rich: possibly a rich believer, possibly a rich outsider
alternatives: a rich believer, humbled by remembering how short life is
a rich unbeliever, whose only "boast" will be his fall (bitter irony)
decisions.reason: The Greek does not repeat "brother" with "the rich". If it carries over, James means a rich believer who should take pride in being brought low. Elsewhere "the rich" in James are outsiders who oppress the church (2:6; 5:1-6), which would make the command ironic. The text leaves it open, and so does this translation.

decisions.choice: like a flower of grass: Isaiah 40:6-8
decisions.reason: "All flesh is grass, and all its beauty is like the flower of the field. The grass withers, the flower fades." James applies Isaiah's picture of human frailty to the rich (also Psalm 103:15-16).

decisions.choice: take pride in; be proud
decisions.reason: καυχάομαι is used here in a good sense. "Boast" in everyday English is almost always bad, so Balanced and Readable say "take pride" and "be proud"; Literal keeps "boast".

decisions.choice: that God has lifted them up
decisions.reason: Readable says who gives the lowly their high place (see the theology decision).

decisions.choice: {{gender:el hermano o la hermana|el hermano}}
decisions.reason: The plural "hermanos" covers men and women without a setting, but the singular "el hermano" names a man. James means any poor believer, so the singular takes the gender setting, as in English. "Humilde" and "le" do not change with gender.

decisions.choice: ajivunie
decisions.reason: "Kujisifu" is bragging, always bad. "Kujivunia" is to take pride in something, which fits the good sense of the Greek word (see the English decision), so Swahili uses the same verb at every level.

decisions.choice: nyasi
decisions.reason: "Majani" can mean both grass and leaves; "nyasi" is grass only, the picture of Isaiah 40 (see the meaning decision). It is used again in verse 11.

source.text: ἀνέτειλεν γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος σὺν τῷ καύσωνι καὶ ἐξήρανεν τὸν χόρτον, καὶ τὸ ἄνθος αὐτοῦ ἐξέπεσεν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἀπώλετο· οὕτως καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν ταῖς πορείαις αὐτοῦ μαρανθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: For rose the sun with the burning heat and dried up the grass, and the flower of it fell and the beauty of the face of it perished; so also the rich in the goings of him will wither away.

en.L: For the sun rose with the scorching heat and dried up the grass, and its flower fell and the beauty of its appearance perished; so also the rich [one] will wither away in {{gender:their|his}} goings.
en.B: The sun comes up with its burning heat and parches the grass; its flower drops, and all its loveliness is gone. That is how the rich will fade away, even while they are busy with their affairs.
en.R: The sun rises, and its heat burns the grass until it dries up. Its flowers fall off, and their beauty is gone. Rich people are like that. They will fade away while they are still busy going about their business.

es.L: Porque salió el sol con el calor abrasador y secó la hierba, y su flor se cayó y la belleza de su aspecto pereció; así también el rico se marchitará en sus andanzas.
es.B: El sol sale con su calor ardiente y seca la hierba; su flor se cae y toda su hermosura se pierde. Así se marchitarán los ricos, aun mientras andan ocupados en sus negocios.
es.R: Sale el sol, y su calor quema la hierba hasta secarla. Sus flores se caen, y su belleza desaparece. Así les pasa a los ricos. Se marchitarán mientras siguen ocupados en sus negocios.

sw.L: Kwa maana jua lilipanda pamoja na joto kali na kuzikausha nyasi, na ua lake likadondoka, na urembo wa sura yake ukaangamia; hivyo hivyo pia tajiri atanyauka katikati ya safari zake.
sw.B: Jua linapanda na joto lake kali na kuzikausha nyasi; ua lake linadondoka, na urembo wake wote unatoweka. Ndivyo matajiri watakavyonyauka, hata wakiwa katikati ya shughuli zao.
sw.R: Jua linapochomoza, joto lake huchoma nyasi hadi zinakauka. Maua yake huanguka, na uzuri wake unatoweka. Ndivyo ilivyo kwa matajiri. Watanyauka wakiwa bado wanahangaika na biashara zao.

decisions.choice: past tenses describing what always happens
decisions.reason: The verbs are past tenses, but they describe the way things always go, as a proverb does. James is telling a little story of every summer's day.

decisions.choice: burning heat: the heat of the sun, perhaps the hot desert wind
decisions.reason: καύσων means burning heat. It can also name the hot east wind that dries up plants in the land of Israel (Jonah 4:8; Ezekiel 17:10). Either way, the grass dies quickly.

decisions.choice: goings: journeys and business, a busy life of getting and spending
decisions.reason: πορεία means a journey or a going. It fits the traveling merchants of 4:13 ("we will go to such a city and trade"). The rich fade away in the middle of their plans.

decisions.choice: present tenses: comes up, parches, drops, is gone
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the proverb-like past tenses into the present, which is how English tells what always happens. Literal keeps the past.

source.text: Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὃς ὑπομένει πειρασμόν, ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήμψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς, ὃν ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [is the] man who endures trial, because approved having become he will receive the crown of the life which he promised to the [ones] loving him.

en.L: Blessed [is] {{gender:the person|the man}} who endures trial, because, having been approved, {{gender:they|he}} will receive the crown of life, which [God] promised to those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Blessed is anyone who endures through trial. When {{gender:they have|he has}} been proved genuine, {{gender:they|he}} will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: God blesses the person who keeps enduring through trials. When that person has been tested and proved true, {{gender:they|he}} will receive the crown of life. God has promised this prize to everyone who loves {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: {{gender:Bienaventurada la persona|Bienaventurado el hombre}} que persevera en [la] prueba, porque, habiendo sido {{gender:aprobada|aprobado}}, recibirá la corona de la vida, que [Dios] prometió a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aman.
es.B: Bienaventurado quien persevera en la prueba. Cuando haya pasado la prueba, recibirá la corona de la vida que Dios ha prometido a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aman.
es.R: Dios bendice a quien sigue perseverando en las pruebas. Cuando haya pasado la prueba y se vea que su fe es verdadera, recibirá la corona de la vida. Dios ha prometido este premio a todos los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aman.

sw.L: Heri mtu anayestahimili jaribu, kwa maana baada ya kuthibitika kuwa halisi, atapewa taji la uzima, ambalo [Mungu] aliahidi kwa wale wanaompenda.
sw.B: Heri mtu anayestahimili wakati wa jaribu. Akishathibitishwa kuwa halisi, atapokea taji la uzima ambalo Mungu amewaahidi wale wanaompenda.
sw.R: Mungu humbariki mtu anayeendelea kustahimili majaribu. Mtu huyo akishajaribiwa na kuonekana kuwa wa kweli, atapokea taji la uzima. Mungu ameahidi tuzo hiyo kwa wote wanaompenda.

decisions.choice: blessed: favored by God and truly well off
decisions.reason: μακάριος is the word of Psalm 1:1 and of Jesus' beatitudes (Matthew 5:3-12). It declares that God's favor rests on such a person, whatever the present feels like.

decisions.choice: trial: the hardship that tests faith, as in verse 2
decisions.reason: πειρασμός keeps the sense of verse 2: the person endures hardship. Verse 13 then turns to the verb in the sense "tempt".

decisions.choice: the crown of life: the victor's wreath, which is life itself
alternatives: a crown belonging to eternal life
decisions.reason: στέφανος is the wreath given to a winner in the games or to someone honored (1 Corinthians 9:25). "Of life" most likely says what the wreath is: the prize is life (Revelation 2:10).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "which he promised", with no named subject
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "the Lord" or "God" to make the subject clear; the SBLGNT, with the oldest manuscripts, has no named subject. Either way God is the one who promised. This description is from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:the person|the man}}; {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: ἀνήρ ("man") is used here of any believer who endures, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: God has promised
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who promised (see the text decision); Literal supplies [God] in brackets.

decisions.choice: God blesses the person
decisions.reason: Readable turns the declaration into a plain statement of who gives the blessing (see the meaning decision on "blessed").

decisions.choice: persevera
decisions.reason: The verb belongs to the same family as "perseverancia" in verses 3-4, so Spanish uses "perseverar" to keep James's thread (also 5:11).

decisions.choice: {{gender:Bienaventurada la persona|Bienaventurado el hombre}}; {{gender:aprobada|aprobado}}
decisions.reason: At Literal the noun takes the gender setting, and the participle must agree with it, so it has a span too. Balanced and Readable say "quien", which needs no setting.

source.text: μηδεὶς πειραζόμενος λεγέτω ὅτι Ἀπὸ θεοῦ πειράζομαι· ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἀπείραστός ἐστιν κακῶν, πειράζει δὲ αὐτὸς οὐδένα.

records.literal_gloss: No one being tempted let say that: From God I am being tempted; for the God untemptable is of evils, and tempts he himself no one.

en.L: Let no one who is being tempted say, "I am being tempted by God"; for God is untempted by evil [things], and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} tempts no one.
en.B: No one who is tempted should say, "God is tempting me." For God is beyond the reach of evil's temptation, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never tempts anyone.
en.R: When you are tempted to do wrong, do not say, "God is tempting me." Evil cannot tempt God, and God never tempts anyone to do wrong.

es.L: Nadie que sea tentado diga: «Soy tentado por Dios»; porque Dios no puede ser tentado por [cosas] malas, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo no tienta a nadie.
es.B: Nadie que sea tentado debe decir: «Dios me está tentando». Porque Dios está fuera del alcance de la tentación del mal, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nunca tienta a nadie.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:sientan|sintáis}} la tentación de hacer el mal, no {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: «Dios me está tentando». El mal no puede tentar a Dios, y Dios nunca tienta a nadie a hacer el mal.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote anayejaribiwa na asiseme kwamba, "Ninajaribiwa kutoka kwa Mungu"; kwa sababu Mungu hajaribiki na mambo maovu, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} mwenyewe hamjaribu yeyote.
sw.B: Mtu anapojaribiwa, asidai kwamba, "Mungu ananijaribu." Kwa maana uovu hauwezi kumvuta Mungu, wala {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hamjaribu mtu yeyote kamwe.
sw.R: Mnapojaribiwa kutenda mabaya, msiseme, "Mungu ananijaribu." Uovu hauwezi kumjaribu Mungu, na Mungu hamjaribu mtu yeyote atende mabaya.

decisions.choice: tempt: draw someone toward sin
decisions.reason: πειράζω belongs to the same family as the "trials" of verses 2 and 12. Here the meaning shifts from testing to enticing toward evil, and verse 14 shows what kind: being dragged off by one's own desire. James blocks the excuse that the trial God allows is God pushing a person to sin.

decisions.choice: untempted by evil: God is not open to the pull of evil
alternatives: God ought not to be put to the test by evil people
decisions.reason: ἀπείραστος occurs only here in the New Testament. It most naturally means that evil has nothing in God that it can pull on, which is why he does not tempt anyone either.

decisions.choice: from God: God as the source, even if not directly
decisions.reason: Ἀπὸ ("from") names where the temptation is said to come from, so it rules out blaming God even indirectly.

decisions.choice: God tests but does not tempt
decisions.reason: Scripture says God tested Abraham (Genesis 22:1), and Jesus taught his followers to pray "do not lead us into temptation" (Matthew 6:13). James's point is that God never draws anyone toward evil.

decisions.choice: tempted, tempting, tempts
decisions.reason: English needs two words where the Greek has one family: "trials" in verses 2 and 12, "tempt" from here on, as the sense shifts (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: to do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what the temptation is toward, so it is not confused with the trials of verses 2-12.

decisions.choice: kujaribu, kujaribiwa
decisions.reason: English needs "trial" and "tempt" for one Greek word family; Swahili "jaribu" covers both testing and tempting, so it keeps the Greek link between verses 2, 12 and 13 ("majaribu", "jaribu", "anayejaribiwa"). Readable adds "kutenda mabaya" to show that the pull toward sin is meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns (yeye, wake, yake)
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("hamjaribu", "wanaompenda"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English in this letter.

source.text: ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος·

records.literal_gloss: But each is tempted by the own desire being dragged off and being lured;

en.L: But each one is tempted by {{gender:their|his}} own desire, being dragged away and lured;
en.B: Rather, each person is tempted by {{gender:their|his}} own desire, which draws {{gender:them|him}} out and lures {{gender:them|him}} like bait.
en.R: People are tempted by the wrong things they want. Their own desires pull them away and trap them, the way bait catches a fish.

es.L: Sino que cada uno es tentado por su propio deseo, siendo arrastrado y seducido;
es.B: Más bien, cada uno es tentado por su propio deseo, que lo arrastra y lo atrae como un cebo.
es.R: Las personas son tentadas por las cosas malas que desean. Sus propios deseos las arrastran y las atrapan, como el cebo atrapa a un pez.

sw.L: Lakini kila mmoja hujaribiwa na tamaa yake mwenyewe, akivutwa mbali na kunaswa kwa chambo;
sw.B: Badala yake, kila mtu hujaribiwa na tamaa yake mwenyewe, inayomvuta na kumnasa kama chambo.
sw.R: Watu hujaribiwa na mambo mabaya wanayoyatamani. Tamaa zao wenyewe huwavuta mbali na kuwanasa, kama chambo kinavyomnasa samaki.

decisions.choice: desire: here, craving for what is wrong
decisions.reason: ἐπιθυμία can be a good desire (Philippians 1:23), but here it gives birth to sin (verse 15), so it is desire turned toward wrong.

decisions.choice: dragged off and lured: hunting and fishing words
decisions.reason: ἐξέλκω means to drag out, as prey is drawn from cover, and δελεάζω means to catch with bait (2 Peter 2:14, 18). Desire is pictured as the bait on the hook.

decisions.choice: own: the source is inside the person, not God
decisions.reason: "Own" (ἰδίας) answers the excuse of verse 13: temptation arises from what a person wants.

decisions.choice: the wrong things they want; the way bait catches a fish
decisions.reason: Readable says that the desire is for wrong things and spells out the fishing picture.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Each one" means everyone, so the pronouns take the gender setting.

source.text: εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν, ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον.

records.literal_gloss: Then the desire having conceived bears sin, and the sin having been completed gives birth to death.

en.L: Then desire, having conceived, bears sin, and sin, having come to full growth, gives birth to death.
en.B: Desire conceives and bears sin, and sin, once it is full grown, gives birth to death.
en.R: Wrong desire is like a mother. It grows inside a person and is born as sin. Then sin grows up, and it gives birth to death.

es.L: Luego el deseo, habiendo concebido, da a luz [el] pecado, y el pecado, habiendo llegado a su pleno desarrollo, hace nacer [la] muerte.
es.B: El deseo concibe y da a luz el pecado, y el pecado, cuando ha crecido del todo, hace nacer la muerte.
es.R: El mal deseo es como una madre. Crece dentro de la persona y da a luz el pecado. Luego el pecado crece y da a luz la muerte.

sw.L: Kisha tamaa, baada ya kushika mimba, huzaa dhambi; nayo dhambi, ikishakua kikamilifu, huzaa kifo.
sw.B: Tamaa hushika mimba na kuzaa dhambi, na dhambi ikishakua kabisa huzaa kifo.
sw.R: Tamaa mbaya ni kama mama. Inakua ndani ya mtu na kuzaliwa kama dhambi. Kisha dhambi inakua, nayo inazaa kifo.

decisions.choice: a chain of births: desire conceives, sin is born, death is born
decisions.reason: James turns the picture from fishing to childbirth. Desire is the mother of sin, and sin, when grown, is the mother of death (Romans 6:23).

decisions.choice: fully grown: come to maturity, having run its course
decisions.reason: ἀποτελέω means brought to completion. Sin grows up like a child, and what it produces is death.

decisions.choice: gives birth: the same verb God uses in verse 18
decisions.reason: ἀποκυέω ("give birth") occurs only here and in verse 18 in the New Testament. Sin gives birth to death; God gives birth to us by the word of truth. James sets the two births side by side.

decisions.choice: bears; gives birth to
decisions.reason: Two Greek verbs, both for giving birth. "Gives birth to" is kept for the second because the same verb is rendered that way in verse 18.

decisions.choice: da a luz; hace nacer
decisions.reason: "Engendrar" is a father's begetting, but both Greek verbs are a mother's giving birth. "Da a luz" renders the first; "hace nacer" renders the second and is used for the same verb in verse 18, where God gives us birth, so the two births can be compared.

decisions.choice: kuzaa (both verbs); kifo
decisions.reason: Swahili "kuzaa" is the ordinary verb for a mother giving birth and serves for both Greek verbs, and for God in verse 18 ("alituzaa"), so the two births stand side by side as the meaning decision explains. "Kifo" is the everyday word for death; "mauti" is older and literary.

source.text: μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί.

records.literal_gloss: Not be misled, brothers of me beloved.

en.L: Do not be led astray, my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: Do not be fooled, my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.R: My dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, do not let anyone fool you about this.

es.L: No {{plural_you:se extravíen|os extraviéis}}, hermanos míos amados.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se dejen|os dejéis}} engañar, mis queridos hermanos.
es.R: Mis queridos hermanos, no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie {{plural_you:los|os}} engañe en esto.

sw.L: Msipotoshwe, ndugu zangu wapendwa.
sw.B: Msikubali kudanganywa, ndugu zangu wapenzi.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu wapendwa, msikubali mtu yeyote awadanganye kuhusu jambo hili.

decisions.choice: a hinge: points back to verses 13-15 and forward to verse 17
decisions.reason: The warning closes the argument that God does not tempt, and opens the positive statement that every good gift comes from him.

decisions.choice: be misled: wander from the truth, be deceived
decisions.reason: πλανάω means to lead someone off the path. The error in view is thinking of God as a source of evil.

decisions.choice: my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James speaks to the whole church, men and women, so the gender setting applies; the traditional "brothers" is the alternative. ἀγαπητοί is "loved": "my dear" says it in everyday words.

source.text: Πᾶσα δόσις ἀγαθὴ καὶ πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον ἄνωθέν ἐστιν, καταβαῖνον ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν φώτων, παρ’ ᾧ οὐκ ἔνι παραλλαγὴ ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα.

records.literal_gloss: Every giving good and every gift perfect from above is, coming down from the Father of the lights, with whom not there is variation or of turning shadow.

en.L: Every good giving and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.
en.B: Every good act of giving and every perfect gift is from above. It comes down from the Father of the lights in the sky, in whom there is no change, and no shadow cast by turning.
en.R: Every good and perfect gift comes from heaven. It comes down from God the Father, who made the sun, the moon, and the stars. Their light moves and changes, and they cast shifting shadows, but God never changes.

es.L: Toda buena dádiva y todo regalo perfecto es de arriba, y baja del Padre de las luces, en quien no hay variación ni sombra de giro.
es.B: Toda buena acción de dar y todo regalo perfecto viene de arriba. Baja del Padre de las luces del cielo, en quien no hay cambio, ni la sombra que proyecta un giro.
es.R: Todo regalo bueno y perfecto viene del cielo. Baja de Dios Padre, que creó el sol, la luna y las estrellas. Esas luces se mueven y cambian, y sus sombras se desplazan, pero Dios nunca cambia.

sw.L: Kila utoaji mwema na kila zawadi kamilifu ni kutoka juu, ikishuka kutoka kwa Baba wa mianga, ambaye kwake hakuna mabadiliko wala kivuli cha mzunguko.
sw.B: Kila tendo jema la kutoa na kila zawadi kamilifu hutoka juu. Hushuka kutoka kwa Baba wa mianga ya angani, ambaye hana mabadiliko yoyote wala kivuli kinachotokana na mzunguko.
sw.R: Kila zawadi njema na kamilifu hutoka mbinguni. Inashuka kutoka kwa Mungu Baba, aliyeumba jua, mwezi na nyota. Mwanga wa vitu hivyo husogea na kubadilika, na vivuli vyake huhama, lakini Mungu habadiliki kamwe.

decisions.choice: every good giving and every perfect gift: the subject of the sentence
alternatives: every giving is good, and every perfect gift is from above
decisions.reason: The words most naturally form one subject: all good giving comes from above. The opening words of the verse happen to form a line of Greek verse, so James may be using a saying his readers knew.

decisions.choice: the Father of the lights: God, creator of the sun, moon and stars
decisions.reason: God made the lights of the sky (Genesis 1:14-18; Psalm 136:7-9). Calling him their Father shows him as the source of light and of every good thing.

decisions.choice: no variation or shadow of turning: God does not change as the heavenly lights do
decisions.reason: τροπή can mean the turning of the heavenly bodies, and παραλλαγή change or variation. Sun and moon move, wax and wane, and cast moving shadows; God is not like them (Malachi 3:6).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "shadow of turning"
alternatives: "variation that belongs to the turning of a shadow"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts have a slightly different ending here, which makes the last words mean something like "the variation that comes with the turning of a shadow". The sense, that God does not change, is the same. This description is from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the lights in the sky
decisions.reason: Balanced says which lights are meant.

decisions.choice: God the Father, who made the sun, the moon, and the stars. Their light moves and changes...
alternatives: the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture: God made the heavenly lights, and unlike them he does not change.

decisions.choice: mianga
decisions.reason: "Nuru" is light itself, the word kept for light as a figure. James means the heavenly bodies that give light (see the meaning decision), which Swahili calls "mianga"; Balanced adds "ya angani", as the English Balanced adds "in the sky".

source.text: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας, εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἀπαρχήν τινα τῶν αὐτοῦ κτισμάτων.

records.literal_gloss: Having willed he gave birth to us by word of truth, for the to be us firstfruits a certain of the of him creatures.

en.L: Having willed [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave birth to us by [the] word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} creatures.
en.B: It was {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will to give us birth through the word of truth, so that we might be something like the firstfruits among all {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has created.
en.R: God chose to give us new life through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} message of truth. He wanted us to be like the first part of the harvest, which belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the first of everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made.

es.L: Habiéndolo querido, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos hizo nacer por [la] palabra de verdad, para que seamos una especie de primicias de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} criaturas.
es.B: Fue {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad hacernos nacer por medio de la palabra de verdad, para que fuéramos algo así como las primicias de todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha creado.
es.R: Dios quiso darnos vida nueva por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mensaje de verdad. Quería que fuéramos como la primera parte de la cosecha, que le pertenece a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: lo primero de todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha hecho.

sw.L: Kwa kuwa alipenda [hivyo], alituzaa kupitia neno la kweli, ili tuwe aina fulani ya limbuko la viumbe {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}}.
sw.B: Ilikuwa ni mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kutuzaa kupitia neno la kweli, ili tuwe kitu kama limbuko miongoni mwa viumbe {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}} vyote.
sw.R: Mungu aliamua kutupa uzima mpya kupitia ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kweli. Alitaka tuwe kama sehemu ya kwanza ya mavuno, ambayo ni mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: wa kwanza kati ya vitu vyote alivyoviumba.

decisions.choice: gave birth to us: God gave believers new life
decisions.reason: ἀποκυέω is the birth-verb of verse 15, now used of God: against sin's birth of death stands God's birth of a new people by his word (1 Peter 1:23). "Us" and "firstfruits" point to believers as the start of God's new creation, though some read it as God's first creation of humankind.

decisions.choice: having willed: by his own free choice
decisions.reason: βουληθεὶς stands first for emphasis. God's new birth comes from his own will, in contrast with the desire that gives birth to sin (verses 14-15).

decisions.choice: the word of truth: the message of the gospel
decisions.reason: The same phrase names the gospel in Colossians 1:5 and Ephesians 1:13. Verse 21 calls it "the implanted word".

decisions.choice: firstfruits: the first part of the harvest, given to God as a pledge of the rest
decisions.reason: Israel brought the first of each harvest to God (Exodus 23:19; Deuteronomy 26:1-11). Believers are the first share of what God will do for all his creation (Romans 8:19-23).

decisions.choice: God; new life; the first part of the harvest, which belongs to him
alternatives: he gave birth to us; firstfruits
decisions.reason: Readable names God, says what kind of birth this is, and explains "firstfruits".

source.text: Ἴστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί.

records.literal_gloss: Know [this], brothers of me beloved.

en.L: Know [this], my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: Be sure of this, my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.R: My dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, remember this.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sepan|Sabed}} [esto], hermanos míos amados.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} por seguro esto, mis queridos hermanos.
es.R: Mis queridos hermanos, {{plural_you:recuerden|recordad}} esto.

sw.L: Jueni [hili], ndugu zangu wapendwa.
sw.B: Fahamuni hili kwa hakika, ndugu zangu wapendwa.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu wapendwa, kumbukeni jambo hili.

decisions.choice: know this: a command
alternatives: "you know [this]", a statement about what they already know
decisions.reason: Ἴστε can be a command or a statement; the forms are the same. As a command it calls attention to what follows; as a statement it points back to what God has done (verse 18).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "know"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read a different word meaning "so then", which joins this verse to verse 18; the oldest manuscripts read "know". This description is from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James speaks to the whole church, men and women, so the gender setting applies; the traditional "brothers" is the alternative. ἀγαπητοί is "loved": "my dear" says it in everyday words.

source.text: ἔστω δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι, βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν, ὀργὴ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς δικαιοσύνην θεοῦ οὐκ ἐργάζεται.

records.literal_gloss: And let be every man swift to the hearing, slow to the speaking, slow to anger; \v 20 for anger of man righteousness of God not works.

en.L: And let {{gender:every person|every man}} be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger; \v 20 for {{gender:a person's|a man's}} anger does not work [the] righteousness of God.
en.B: Every person should be eager to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger, \v 20 for {{gender:human anger|a man's anger}} does not accomplish the righteousness of God.
en.R: Everyone should be quick to listen and slow to speak. Do not be quick to get angry. \v 20 When people are angry, they do not live the righteous life that God wants.

es.L: Y que {{gender:todo ser humano|todo hombre}} sea pronto para oír, lento para hablar, lento para [la] ira; \v 20 porque la ira {{gender:del ser humano|del hombre}} no obra [la] justicia de Dios.
es.B: Toda persona debe estar dispuesta a escuchar, ser lenta para hablar y lenta para enojarse, \v 20 porque la ira {{gender:humana|del hombre}} no produce la justicia de Dios.
es.R: Todos deben estar listos para escuchar y ser lentos para hablar. No {{plural_you:se enojen|os enfadéis}} enseguida. \v 20 Cuando la gente se enoja, no vive la vida justa que Dios quiere.

sw.L: Na kila mwanadamu na awe mwepesi katika kusikia, mzito katika kusema, mzito katika kukasirika; \v 20 kwa maana hasira ya mtu haitendi haki ya Mungu.
sw.B: Kila mtu anapaswa kuwa tayari kusikiliza, kuchelewa kusema, na kuchelewa kukasirika, \v 20 kwa sababu hasira ya mwanadamu haitimizi haki ya Mungu.
sw.R: Kila mtu awe tayari kusikiliza na asiwe na haraka ya kusema. Msiwe wepesi wa kukasirika. \v 20 Watu wanapokasirika, hawaishi maisha ya haki ambayo Mungu anataka.

decisions.choice: the righteousness of God: the right conduct God requires and approves
alternatives: God's justice, which human anger thinks it is carrying out
decisions.reason: James is speaking about how believers live: anger does not produce the life God counts right. The phrase can also mean God's own justice, which no angry person brings about on God's behalf.

decisions.choice: anger: settled human anger, quick temper
decisions.reason: ὀργή is the anger of the person "slow to anger" in verse 19; the wisdom books warn against it (Proverbs 14:29; Ecclesiastes 7:9).

decisions.choice: quick to hear, slow to speak: Israel's wisdom
decisions.reason: Proverbs says the same: the many words of a fool (Proverbs 10:19; 29:20) and the soft answer that turns away wrath (Proverbs 15:1).

decisions.choice: every person; a man: anyone at all
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπος is the general word for a human being; ἀνήρ usually means a man, but in James's sayings it stands for anyone (1:8, 1:12).

decisions.choice: {{gender:every person|every man}}; {{gender:a person's|a man's}}
decisions.reason: The sayings are for everyone, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: they do not live the righteous life that God wants
alternatives: does not produce the righteousness of God
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of righteousness is meant (see the theology decision).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:se enojen|os enfadéis}}
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the readers, as the English Readable does. The setting also uses each region's everyday verb: "enojarse" in Latin America, "enfadarse" in Spain.

decisions.choice: hasira, kukasirika
decisions.reason: This is human anger, so Swahili says "hasira"; "ghadhabu" is kept for the wrath of God, as in Romans.

source.text: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν ἔμφυτον λόγον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore having put off all filthiness and excess of wickedness in gentleness receive the implanted word the [one] being able to save the souls of you.

en.L: Therefore, having put off all filthiness and [the] excess of wickedness, in gentleness receive the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
en.B: So take off all that is filthy and the wickedness that overflows, and with a gentle spirit welcome the word rooted in you, which has the power to save your souls.
en.R: So get rid of everything dirty and evil in your lives. Be humble, and welcome the message that God has planted in your hearts. It has the power to save you.

es.L: Por tanto, quitándo{{plural_you:se|os}} toda suciedad y [la] abundancia de maldad, {{plural_you:reciban|recibid}} con mansedumbre la palabra plantada, la que puede salvar {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} almas.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:quítense|quitaos}} todo lo sucio y la maldad que se desborda, y con un espíritu manso {{plural_you:acojan|acoged}} la palabra plantada en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que tiene poder para salvar {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} almas.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} todo lo sucio y malo que hay en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida. {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} humildes y {{plural_you:reciban|recibid}} el mensaje que Dios ha plantado en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón. Ese mensaje tiene poder para {{plural_you:salvarlos|salvaros}}.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo, mkishavua kila uchafu na wingi wa uovu, karibisheni kwa upole neno lililopandwa [ndani yenu], lenye uwezo wa kuokoa nafsi zenu.
sw.B: Basi vueni kila kitu kichafu na uovu unaofurika, na kwa roho ya upole mlipokee neno lililopandwa ndani yenu, ambalo lina nguvu ya kuokoa nafsi zenu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo achaneni na kila kitu kichafu na kiovu maishani mwenu. Muwe wanyenyekevu, mkaukaribishe ujumbe ambao Mungu ameupanda mioyoni mwenu. Ujumbe huo una nguvu ya kuwaokoa.

decisions.choice: put off: as one takes off dirty clothes
decisions.reason: ἀποτίθημι is used for taking off clothing, and the New Testament uses it for leaving behind the old way of life (Colossians 3:8; Ephesians 4:22). "Filthiness" is the word for dirty clothes in 2:2.

decisions.choice: excess of wickedness: the evil that overflows
alternatives: what is left over of wickedness
decisions.reason: περισσεία means abundance or surplus. It describes wickedness that spills over, especially in angry words (verses 19-20).

decisions.choice: implanted: planted within by God
decisions.reason: ἔμφυτος can mean inborn, but here the word is received, so it has been planted from outside. It is the word of truth of verse 18, and recalls God's promise to put his law within his people (Jeremiah 31:33).

decisions.choice: souls: the whole person, saved at the last day
decisions.reason: ψυχή here is the person as a whole, before God. The salvation in view is final rescue from death and judgment, as in 5:20.

decisions.choice: save you
decisions.reason: Readable says "you", since "soul" here means the whole person (see the meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep "souls".

decisions.choice: with a gentle spirit
decisions.reason: πραΰτης is the gentleness that stands against anger (verse 20); "meekness" is no longer everyday English.

decisions.choice: kuvua
decisions.reason: "Kuvua" is the verb for taking off clothes, which keeps the picture of the meaning decision (dirty clothes put off). Readable says plainly "achaneni na".

source.text: Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And become doers of word and not hearers only deceiving yourselves.

en.L: And become doers of [the] word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.
en.B: Be people who carry out the word, not just people who hear it. Otherwise you are fooling yourselves.
en.R: Hearing God's message is not enough. You must also do what it says, or you are only tricking yourselves.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:sean|sed}} hacedores de [la] palabra y no solamente oidores, {{plural_you:engañándose a sí mismos|engañándoos a vosotros mismos}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} personas que ponen por obra la palabra, no solo que la oyen. De lo contrario, {{plural_you:se engañan a sí mismos|os engañáis a vosotros mismos}}.
es.R: No basta con oír el mensaje de Dios. También {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que hacer lo que dice, o solo {{plural_you:se están engañando|os estáis engañando}} a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos.

sw.L: Na iweni watendaji wa neno, si wasikilizaji peke yake, mkijidanganya wenyewe.
sw.B: Muwe watu wanaolitekeleza neno, si watu wanaolisikia tu. La sivyo mnajidanganya wenyewe.
sw.R: Kusikia ujumbe wa Mungu hakutoshi. Ni lazima pia mfanye unavyosema, la sivyo mnajidanganya tu.

decisions.choice: doers: people whose lives carry out what they hear
decisions.reason: ποιητής is one who does. Paul makes the same point: not the hearers of the law but the doers are right with God (Romans 2:13). Jesus ends the Sermon on the Mount with it (Matthew 7:24-27).

decisions.choice: hearers: Scripture was mostly heard, read aloud in the gathering
decisions.reason: Few people owned books; the word was heard in synagogue and church. A "hearer" was a member of the listening congregation.

decisions.choice: deceiving yourselves: reasoning yourselves into a false belief
decisions.reason: παραλογίζομαι means to deceive by false reasoning: thinking that hearing is enough.

decisions.choice: people who carry out the word; people who hear it
decisions.reason: "Doers" and "hearers" are not natural English nouns; Balanced says the same with "people who". Literal keeps the nouns.

source.text: ὅτι εἴ τις ἀκροατὴς λόγου ἐστὶν καὶ οὐ ποιητής, οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ, κατενόησεν γὰρ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν.

records.literal_gloss: Because if anyone a hearer of word is and not a doer, this one is like a man looking at the face of the birth of him in a mirror; \v 24 for he looked at himself and has gone away and immediately forgot of what sort he was.

en.L: For if anyone is a hearer of [the] word and not a doer, this [one] is like a man looking closely at his natural face in a mirror; \v 24 for he looked at himself and has gone away, and at once forgot what he was like.
en.B: Anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man studying his own face in a mirror. \v 24 He looks himself over, goes away, and at once forgets what he looked like.
en.R: Some people hear God's message but do not do what it says. They are like a man who looks at his face in a mirror. \v 24 He sees himself, then walks away, and soon he cannot remember what his face was like.

es.L: Porque si alguno es oidor de [la] palabra y no hacedor, este se parece a un hombre que observa atentamente su rostro natural en un espejo; \v 24 porque se observó a sí mismo y se ha ido, y enseguida olvidó cómo era.
es.B: Quien oye la palabra pero no la pone por obra es como un hombre que se mira detenidamente la cara en un espejo. \v 24 Se observa, se va, y enseguida olvida cómo era su aspecto.
es.R: Algunas personas oyen el mensaje de Dios, pero no hacen lo que dice. Son como un hombre que se mira la cara en un espejo. \v 24 Se ve, luego se va, y pronto ya no recuerda cómo era su cara.

sw.L: Kwa sababu mtu yeyote akiwa msikilizaji wa neno wala si mtendaji, huyo ni kama mtu anayeutazama kwa makini uso aliozaliwa nao katika kioo; \v 24 kwa maana alijiangalia, akaondoka, na papo hapo akasahau jinsi alivyokuwa.
sw.B: Mtu anayesikia neno lakini hatendi linavyosema ni kama mtu anayechunguza uso wake katika kioo. \v 24 Anajiangalia, anaondoka, na mara moja anasahau sura yake ilivyokuwa.
sw.R: Watu wengine husikia ujumbe wa Mungu lakini hawafanyi unavyosema. Wao ni kama mtu anayejiangalia uso katika kioo. \v 24 Anajiona, kisha anaondoka, na baada ya muda mfupi hakumbuki uso wake ulivyokuwa.

decisions.choice: look at: observe carefully, not glance
decisions.reason: κατανοέω means to look attentively. The man does look carefully; the fault is that he walks away and forgets. Verse 25 sets against him the one who keeps looking.

decisions.choice: the face of his birth: his natural face, the face he was born with
alternatives: his true self, the person he really is
decisions.reason: "Of his birth" (γενέσεως) means the face he has by nature. Some see a hint of a person's true self, but the picture is first of all an ordinary face in a mirror.

decisions.choice: mirror: polished metal, giving a dim picture
decisions.reason: Mirrors were made of polished bronze or other metal (1 Corinthians 13:12).

decisions.choice: looked, has gone away, forgot: quick, vivid succession
decisions.reason: The verbs switch between past and perfect, which makes the little scene lively: a look, a departure, and the face is gone.

decisions.choice: a man
decisions.reason: ἀνήρ is "man". He is a figure in a picture, not a general statement about people, so no gender setting is used and the pronouns stay "he" and "his".

decisions.choice: mtu
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "man", and the English keeps "a man" because he is a figure in a picture. Swahili "mtu" (a person) tells the picture just as well, and "mwanamume" would stress that he is male, which is not the point.

decisions.choice: uso aliozaliwa nao
decisions.reason: "The face he was born with" keeps the Greek "of his birth" and means his natural face, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ὁ δὲ παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας, οὐκ ἀκροατὴς ἐπιλησμονῆς γενόμενος ἀλλὰ ποιητὴς ἔργου, οὗτος μακάριος ἐν τῇ ποιήσει αὐτοῦ ἔσται.

records.literal_gloss: But the [one] having looked into law perfect the of the freedom and having stayed, not a hearer of forgetfulness having become but a doer of work, this one blessed in the doing of him will be.

en.L: But the one who has looked into [the] perfect law, the [law] of freedom, and has stayed [with it], having become not a hearer who forgets but a doer of [the] work, this [one] will be blessed in {{gender:their|his}} doing.
en.B: But whoever looks closely into the perfect law of freedom and stays with it, not hearing and then forgetting but doing the work, will be blessed in what {{gender:they do|he does}}.
en.R: But some people look closely into God's perfect law, the law of freedom, and they keep on looking. They do not forget what they hear. They do what it says. God will bless them in what they do.

es.L: Pero el que ha mirado atentamente en [la] ley perfecta, la de la libertad, y ha permanecido [en ella], no habiéndose hecho oidor olvidadizo sino hacedor de [la] obra, este será bienaventurado en su hacer.
es.B: Pero quien mira con atención la ley perfecta de la libertad y se queda en ella, no oyendo para luego olvidar, sino haciendo la obra, será bienaventurado en lo que hace.
es.R: Pero hay personas que miran con atención la ley perfecta de Dios, la ley que da libertad, y siguen mirándola. No olvidan lo que oyen. Hacen lo que dice. Dios las bendecirá en lo que hacen.

sw.L: Lakini yule aliyeinama kuchungulia katika sheria kamilifu, ile ya uhuru, na akaendelea [nayo], akiwa si msikilizaji anayesahau bali mtendaji wa kazi, huyo atakuwa heri katika utendaji wake.
sw.B: Lakini mtu anayechunguza kwa makini sheria kamilifu ya uhuru na kuendelea nayo, asiyesikia kisha akasahau bali anayetenda kazi inayotakiwa, atabarikiwa katika kile anachofanya.
sw.R: Lakini watu wengine huichunguza kwa makini sheria kamilifu ya Mungu, sheria inayoleta uhuru, nao huendelea kuitazama. Hawasahau wanachosikia. Wanafanya inavyosema. Mungu atawabariki katika yale wanayofanya.

decisions.choice: looked into: bent down to look closely
decisions.reason: παρακύπτω is used of stooping to look into the empty tomb (John 20:5, 11) and of angels longing to look into the gospel (1 Peter 1:12). It is a close, intent look, and "stayed" says the person keeps looking.

decisions.choice: the perfect law of freedom: God's law as received and fulfilled in Jesus' teaching
alternatives: a principle of freedom with no commands
decisions.reason: The "law" is God's law, which James quotes in 2:8-11 and calls "the royal law". It is "perfect" (complete, Psalm 19:7) and "of freedom" because it is the word planted in the heart (verse 21), which sets people free rather than enslaving them (Psalm 119:45; John 8:31-32).

decisions.choice: a hearer of forgetfulness: a forgetful hearer
decisions.reason: The genitive describes the kind of hearer: one marked by forgetting, like the man at the mirror.

decisions.choice: will be blessed: in the doing itself, and at the end
decisions.reason: The future "will be" looks ahead to God's blessing, but "in his doing" places it in the very act of obeying (John 13:17).

decisions.choice: They do what it says
decisions.reason: ἔργον here is the doing the law asks for. Readable says it plainly instead of "work".

decisions.choice: God will bless them in what they do
alternatives: will be blessed in their doing
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who blesses.

decisions.choice: aliyeinama kuchungulia
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is stooping to look closely (see the meaning decision); Literal says "bent down to peer into". Balanced and Readable say "anachunguza kwa makini" (examines carefully).

source.text: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ θρησκὸς εἶναι μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, τούτου μάταιος ἡ θρησκεία.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone thinks religious to be not bridling tongue of him but deceiving heart of him, of this one worthless the religion.

en.L: If anyone thinks {{gender:they are|he is}} religious, not bridling {{gender:their|his}} tongue but deceiving {{gender:their|his}} heart, this person's religion is worthless.
en.B: If anyone thinks {{gender:they are|he is}} devout but does not put a bridle on {{gender:their|his}} tongue, {{gender:they are|he is}} fooling {{gender:themselves|himself}}, and {{gender:their|his}} religion is empty.
en.R: Some people think they serve God well, but they do not control what they say. They are fooling themselves, and their religion is worth nothing.

es.L: Si alguien cree ser religioso, sin refrenar su lengua sino engañando a su corazón, la religión de ese es vana.
es.B: Si alguien se cree piadoso, pero no le pone freno a su lengua, se engaña a sí mismo, y su religión está vacía.
es.R: Algunas personas creen que sirven bien a Dios, pero no controlan lo que dicen. Se engañan a sí mismas, y su religión no vale nada.

sw.L: Ikiwa mtu anajiona kuwa mtu wa dini, bila kuutia ulimi wake hatamu, bali akiudanganya moyo wake, dini ya huyo ni bure.
sw.B: Mtu akijiona kuwa mcha Mungu lakini hauwekei ulimi wake hatamu, anajidanganya mwenyewe, na dini yake ni tupu.
sw.R: Watu wengine hudhani kwamba wanamtumikia Mungu vizuri, lakini hawazuii maneno yao. Wanajidanganya wenyewe, na dini yao haina thamani yoyote.

decisions.choice: religious, religion: the outward practice of worship
decisions.reason: θρησκεία is the practice of religion: worship, prayer, keeping rituals (Acts 26:5). James does not reject it but asks what true practice looks like (verse 27).

decisions.choice: thinks: considers himself
decisions.reason: δοκέω can mean "seem" or "think". With "deceiving his heart" it is the person's own opinion of himself that is at fault.

decisions.choice: bridle the tongue: control speech as a rider controls a horse
decisions.reason: χαλιναγωγέω means to guide with a bridle. James develops the picture in 3:2-3.

decisions.choice: worthless: empty, achieving nothing
decisions.reason: μάταιος means futile; it is used of idols and empty ways (Acts 14:15; 1 Peter 1:18).

decisions.choice: fooling themselves
decisions.reason: "Heart" is the person within; Balanced and Readable say "themselves". Literal keeps "heart".

decisions.choice: kuutia ulimi hatamu
decisions.reason: "Hatamu" is a bridle, so Literal and Balanced keep James's picture of a rider controlling a horse, which he develops in 3:2-3. Readable says plainly "hawazuii maneno yao".

source.text: θρησκεία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος παρὰ τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ αὕτη ἐστίν, ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν τῇ θλίψει αὐτῶν, ἄσπιλον ἑαυτὸν τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: Religion pure and undefiled before the God and Father this is, to visit orphans and widows in the affliction of them, unstained oneself to keep from the world.

en.L: Religion pure and undefiled before [our] God and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, [and] to keep oneself unstained from the world.
en.B: To God the Father, religion that is pure and untainted looks like this: going to the help of orphans and widows in their trouble, and keeping yourself unstained by the world.
en.R: Here is the kind of religion that God the Father sees as pure and good: caring for orphans and widows when they are suffering, and not letting the world's evil make you dirty.

es.L: [La] religión pura e incontaminada delante del Dios y Padre es esta: visitar a [los] huérfanos y a [las] viudas en su aflicción, [y] guardarse a sí mismo sin mancha del mundo.
es.B: Para Dios el Padre, la religión pura y sin contaminación es esta: acudir en ayuda de los huérfanos y de las viudas en sus dificultades, y mantenerse sin mancha del mundo.
es.R: Esta es la religión que Dios el Padre considera pura y buena: cuidar a los huérfanos y a las viudas cuando sufren, y no dejarse ensuciar por la maldad del mundo.

sw.L: Dini safi isiyotiwa najisi mbele ya Mungu na Baba ni hii: kuwatembelea yatima na wajane katika taabu zao, [na] kujitunza bila doa kutokana na ulimwengu.
sw.B: Mbele ya Mungu Baba, dini iliyo safi na isiyochafuliwa ni hii: kuwasaidia yatima na wajane katika shida zao, na kujiweka mwenyewe bila doa la ulimwengu.
sw.R: Hii ndiyo dini ambayo Mungu Baba anaiona kuwa safi na njema: kuwatunza yatima na wajane wanapoteseka, na kujilinda usichafuliwe na uovu wa ulimwengu.

decisions.choice: visit: come to help and care for
decisions.reason: ἐπισκέπτομαι means to visit with care and help, as for the sick and the prisoner in Matthew 25:36. It is also the word for God visiting his people to save them (Luke 1:68).

decisions.choice: orphans and widows: the most unprotected people in society
decisions.reason: With no father or husband to support them, they had no one to speak for them. God is called their defender (Deuteronomy 10:18; Psalm 68:5), and the prophets judged Israel by how it treated them (Isaiah 1:17).

decisions.choice: the world: human life organized without and against God
decisions.reason: κόσμος here is not the created world but the values and ways opposed to God, as in 4:4 ("friendship with the world is enmity with God").

decisions.choice: God and Father: one person
decisions.reason: One article covers both words: God, who is the Father, the Father of the lights in verse 17.

decisions.choice: pure, undefiled, unstained: words from worship and sacrifice
decisions.reason: Clean and unblemished were the marks of acceptable worship and sacrifice (Leviticus 22:20; 1 Peter 1:19). James says the cleanness God accepts is mercy to the helpless and a life kept clean.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "to keep oneself unstained from the world"
decisions.reason: At least one early papyrus reads a different verb, so that the believers protect the orphans and widows from the world. The SBLGNT follows the great majority of manuscripts. This description is from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: [our] God and Father
decisions.reason: English cannot keep the article here; Literal supplies [our], as the phrase is used elsewhere (Philippians 4:20).

decisions.choice: not letting the world's evil make you dirty
alternatives: keep oneself unstained from the world
decisions.reason: Readable explains the stain picture: the evil of the world (see the meaning decision on "world").

decisions.choice: delante del Dios y Padre
decisions.reason: Spanish can keep the one article over both words ("del Dios y Padre"), so Literal needs no supplied "[nuestro]" as the English does.

decisions.choice: ulimwengu
decisions.reason: "Dunia" is the earth; "ulimwengu" is also the world of people and its ways, which is the sense here (see the meaning decision).
